adjudication_rationale: The introduced part, a claim that a PR into main always runs every suite, is corrected in cc8b59dc0 (docs, changelog, ci.yml). What remains is GitHub's retarget behaviour: a base change reruns no CI. That predates this change, and the docs-only gate has it too with a larger effect. It needs a new workflow that emits a required-check name, which is its own review unit, #4906 (P2). The retarget is also off-process (main is release-only, and a PR into main needs a colleague's approval). The damage further requires a wrong skip, and every known route to one is closed. A push to main runs the full matrix.
waiver_rationale: Residual accepted under the operator's delegation, with the claim corrected and the guard tracked as #4906 (P2).
trigger: A PR into dev gets a verdict that skips a family, and its base is then changed to main with no new push. Default pull_request types exclude `edited`, so CI does not rerun; the dev run's green checks satisfy Protect Main (strict; origin/main is an ancestor of origin/dev), so the merge carries a family that never ran on the head's own changes.
classification_rationale: The changelog and docs said a PR into main always runs every suite; a retargeted PR keeps its dev verdict. The mechanism is pre-existing GitHub behaviour the docs-only gate shares.
summary: Gate 8: the base_ref guard is bypassed by retargeting a dev PR to main without a push. Claim corrected in cc8b59dc0 ('a PR opened against main'; the retarget behaviour is documented); the guard for both gates is #4906 (P2).
